Part of the workspace wave: eliminate ASCII/box-drawing frame diagrams (this slice = celestia-devtools only).

## Claim

Structural diagrams in celestia-devtools docs/reports/PR descriptions are fenced Mermaid blocks, and the markdown linter mechanically rejects box-frame glyph diagrams outside legal fences.

## What

- `docs/<locale>/diagram-policy.md` in nine locales (ar, en, es, fr, ja, ko, ru, zhs, zht): flows, architecture layers, state machines, sequences and timelines must be fenced Mermaid blocks; ASCII/box-drawing frame diagrams are forbidden. Exemptions: directory-tree listings, terminal/console output depictions, plain-text runtime output. The renderable-kinds list and fallback contract point at the authority — entelecheia [`communication-style.md` Language Purity rule 6](https://github.com/celestia-island/entelecheia/blob/master/res/prompts/system/communication-style.md) (graph/flowchart with declared direction TD/TB/BT/LR/RL, stateDiagram(-v2), sequenceDiagram, classDiagram, gantt, pie, quadrantChart; other kinds fall back to a plain code block and are forbidden in rendered docs); that file wins on conflict.
- New check module `src/celestia_devtools/doc/linter/frames.py`, wired into `format-markdown`: fence-aware scan flags box-frame corner/junction glyphs (`┌┐┘┬┴┼╔╗╝╚╠╣╦╩╬┏┓┗┛┣┫`) outside mermaid fences; fences tagged `console`/`terminal`/`ansi`/`output`/`text` are exempt (terminal-output depictions stay legal plain text); the plain tree glyph family (`│ ├ └ ─`, `├── name` listings) is deliberately not flagged. Violations report `file:line` in the existing warning style.
- README "Style Checkers" mentions the new gate in **en only** — the only locale whose README documents the checkers (other locale READMEs have no such section; nothing invented).

## Enforcement

`gate` — `format-markdown` exits 1 on frame glyphs outside mermaid/terminal-output fences (in both `--check` and format modes; a policy breach is not auto-fixable formatting).

## Negative control

The same box-frame glyphs must PASS inside a Mermaid fence, inside every terminal-output fence tag (console/terminal/ansi/output/text), and as a plain directory-tree listing — the gate flags frame art only outside those legal fences and never flags the `│ ├ └ ─` tree glyph family (`tests/test_frames.py::test_negative_controls`, stated in the module docstring).

## No behavior change to existing checks

Formatting, fence-language inference, tab lint and i18n lint keep their flags, outputs and warnings-only severity. The repository tree contains zero frame-glyph violations (the one glyph-bearing markdown file, `tools/README.md`, is a genuine directory tree and stays), so every existing `format-markdown` invocation result is unchanged; `format-markdown . --check` on the full tree exits 0 before and after.
